sources.source_name: Washington State Department of Ecology Air Quality Monitoring Hourly Results
sources.owning_agency: Washington State Department of Ecology Air Quality Program
sources.access_method: HTTPS GET to ArcGIS REST metadata and query endpoints
sources.machine_readable_availability: Yes - JSON / GeoJSON / PBF query support
sources.terms_usage_constraints: Public agency map service; Ecology describes data as near real-time air-monitoring information.
sources.geographic_coverage: Washington statewide; route bbox query returned 4 route-near official monitor sites on July 29, 2026.
route_points_sections_covered: UW / Burke-Gilman west via Seattle-NE 127th monitor
Kenmore / Lake Forest Park north shore via Lake Forest Park-Town Center monitor
Issaquah terminus via Issaquah-Lake Sammamish monitor
sources.available_fields: SiteId, SiteName, SiteLocation, DateTime_PST, AQIValue, AQICategory, pollutant-specific AQI and values for PM2.5 / PM10 / ozone / NO2 / SO2 / CO when present
sources.typical_publication_delay: Near real-time; practical observation delay appeared sub-hourly
sources.historical_availability: Rolling last 24 hours in this service
sources.pagination_behavior: ArcGIS transfer limits apply on broad queries; constrained route-latest query returned 4 rows without pagination
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, JSON parse failure, missing features, stale DateTime_PST, or zero route-near rows
sources.fallback_method: AIRNOW-02 coarse reporting-area data plus stale last-known-good; optionally PSCAA-01 session-backed station detail
sources.research_notes: Best current machine-readable source found. Latest-hour route query returned Seattle-NE 127th, Lake Forest Park-Town Center, Bellevue-SE 12th, and Issaquah-Lake Sammamish rows. PM10 fields existed but were null on all route-near rows during the July 29, 2026 test.

sources.source_name: Washington State Department of Ecology Smoke Forecast
sources.owning_agency: Washington State Department of Ecology Air Quality Program
sources.access_method: HTTPS GET to ArcGIS REST metadata and query endpoints
sources.terms_usage_constraints: Public state smoke-forecast service; use as outlook, not as current observation.
sources.available_fields: SmokeForecastId, Site, SiteName, Season, DisplayFlag, Date, Day1-Day5, ModifiedDate
sources.update_frequency: Service description says updated hourly in the mornings; wildfire page says 5-day forecast in summer and 2-day forecast otherwise
sources.typical_publication_delay: Morning issuance with same-day updates as forecasters adjust
sources.historical_availability: Current forecast run only in this tested path
sources.pagination_behavior: No pagination issue observed on route query
sources.recommended_freshness_threshold: 12 hours in smoke season; 24 hours off-season
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, parse failure, no route-intersecting DisplayFlag=1 polygon, or blank Day1-Day5 values
sources.research_notes: Route bbox intersected a live summer polygon named Seattle-Bellevue-Kent Valley with Good values for Day1-Day5 on July 29, 2026. Strongest official outlook source found.

sources.terms_usage_constraints: AirNow data use guidelines apply; preliminary AQI/reporting data not intended for regulatory use.
sources.geographic_coverage: U.S. / Canada / Mexico reporting areas and site-level services
route_points_sections_covered: Potentially whole route, but reporting-area granularity unless site-level endpoints are used
sources.available_fields: Current observations, forecasts, monitoring-site hourly/daily data depending on endpoint
sources.geometry_availability: Lat/long query inputs; output geometry varies by endpoint
sources.update_frequency: FAQ says observations generally update hourly and forecasts daily
sources.typical_publication_delay: FAQ says previous-hour observations generally available 10-30 minutes past the hour
sources.historical_availability: Yes by separate historical endpoints, not tested with valid credentials in this cycle
sources.documented_rate_limits: Per-key hourly limits exist; no single universal limit quoted in the FAQ
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, AirNow error body, empty payload, or stale timestamps
sources.research_notes: Live invalid-key test returned HTTP 401 JSON Invalid API key, proving the endpoint is live and auth-gated. Useful with credentials, but not required for MVP because Ecology gives stronger official corridor segmentation without credentials.

sources.source_name: AirNow file products: reportingarea.dat and cityzipcodes.csv
sources.machine_readable_availability: Yes - pipe-delimited and CSV file outputs
sources.terms_usage_constraints: AirNow data use guidelines apply; preliminary AQI/reporting data.
sources.geographic_coverage: National reporting areas and reporting-area-to-ZIP mappings
route_points_sections_covered: Most route ZIPs map to Seattle-Bellevue-Kent Valley
Some foothill ZIPs map to Cascade foothills of King County in cityzipcodes.csv
sources.available_fields: Observation/forecast rows with date, time, type flag, reporting area, state, lat/lon, pollutant, AQI, category, action-day flag, forecast discussion; ZIP-to-reporting-area lookup table
sources.geometry_availability: Reporting-area centroid and ZIP centroids only
sources.update_frequency: reportingarea.dat twice per hour at :25 and :55 per AirNow FAQ; cityzipcodes.csv once per day
sources.typical_publication_delay: Observation rows showed a 12:00 PDT snapshot during the July 29, 2026 test
sources.historical_availability: Current-day file products only in this tested path
sources.recommended_freshness_threshold: 90 minutes for observation rows; 24 hours for ZIP mapping
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, empty file, stale observation time, or missing route reporting-area rows
sources.research_notes: Strong national fallback and easiest AirNow path without credentials. Weakness: route resolution is coarse. On July 29, 2026 the route only had live rows for Seattle-Bellevue-Kent Valley, so AirNow alone would understate within-corridor variation.

sources.source_name: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency network map backend
sources.access_method: Cookie-backed HTTPS JSON endpoints discovered from the official network-map page
sources.authentication_requirements: No login, but an ASP.NET session bootstrap cookie is required before station-detail calls succeed
sources.terms_usage_constraints: Official public technical tool; no published API contract or rate-limit doc found.
sources.available_fields: Station list, AQI polygons, station detail including lat/lon, address, county, telemetry status, pollutant/QMU metadata, AQI category
sources.geometry_availability: Point geometry in station detail; polygon geometry in Geometries
sources.update_frequency: Appears near-real-time for current network map; no formal schedule published
sources.historical_availability: Current-state network map only in tested endpoints
sources.failure_detection_method: JSON success:false, session-null message, non-200, or empty item list
sources.research_notes: Strong secondary source, but not chosen as MVP because the best detail endpoint (Aqi) fails statelessly with Session was null, refresh the page. A session bootstrap solved that in live testing.

sources.source_name: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency Air Quality Burn Ban Status
sources.machine_readable_availability: Partial - stable repeated status blocks in HTML, but no documented JSON endpoint found
sources.geographic_coverage: PSCAA burn-ban areas in King / Kitsap / Pierce / Snohomish counties
sources.available_fields: Human-readable ban/no-ban status plus explanatory text and links
sources.geometry_availability: No machine-readable geometry found; separate area map linked
sources.recommended_freshness_threshold: 24 hours, or change-driven during burn-ban season
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, missing status blocks, or page structure change
sources.fallback_method: Agency hotline listed on the same page
sources.research_notes: Best official burn-ban source found. Live HTML contained repeated No Ban status blocks on July 29, 2026.

sources.source_name: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency air-sensor map / air-sensor dashboard
sources.access_method: Public web pages linking to dashboard tools
sources.terms_usage_constraints: Official corrected/QC'd sensor layer; PSCAA warns raw PurpleAir should not be used uncorrected.
route_points_sections_covered: Potentially whole route if machine-readable access is confirmed
sources.available_fields: Official description promises corrected/QC'd low-cost sensor information and confidence values
sources.geometry_availability: Likely yes in the live map, but unattended export/feed was not verified
sources.recommended_freshness_threshold: Not assigned until machine-readable access is proven
sources.research_notes: Officially valuable because PSCAA explicitly documents EPA-calibrated and quality-controlled sensor use, but this cycle did not prove a stable unattended data export path.

sources.owning_agency: Washington Smoke Information partnership led by WA Ecology and partner agencies
sources.terms_usage_constraints: Official partnership blog; use as outlook/context, not as current monitor substitute.
route_points_sections_covered: Whole route at regional outlook level
sources.available_fields: RSS item title, publication time, category tags, content/description
sources.update_frequency: Event-driven; more active during smoke season
sources.historical_availability: Recent RSS items plus full Blogger archive
sources.pagination_behavior: Feed length limit only; no pagination tested
sources.recommended_freshness_threshold: 12 hours in smoke season; 24 hours off-season
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, empty RSS, stale lastBuildDate, or malformed XML
sources.research_notes: Best official prose smoke-outlook feed. Live RSS returned a current lastBuildDate on July 29, 2026.

sources.source_name: National Weather Service active alerts API filtered to Air Quality Alert
sources.terms_usage_constraints: Public NWS API; current alert feed only
route_points_sections_covered: Route relevance determined by county/zone/polygon match to King County and route geometry
sources.available_fields: event, headline, severity, certainty, urgency, areaDesc, effective, expires, senderName, more CAP-derived fields
sources.geometry_availability: Sometimes; tested WA sample had geometry null and relied on area descriptions/geocodes
sources.update_frequency: Event-driven; tested response had cache-control max-age=5
sources.pagination_behavior: No pagination needed for tested WA sample
sources.documented_rate_limits: Standard NWS API guidance; no numeric limit verified in this cycle
sources.failure_detection_method: Non-200, empty features when an alert is expected, stale updated, or parse failure
sources.last_known_good_suitability: Yes, but expired alerts must be dropped promptly
sources.fallback_method: WASMOKE-01 plus ECO-02 plus PSCAA-02 depending on the use case
sources.research_notes: Good official alert channel for formal advisory states. On July 29, 2026 the route had no King County air-quality alert, but live WA sample data existed for eastern Washington and proved the schema.

sources.source_name: Public Health - Seattle & King County wildfire smoke guidance
route_points_sections_covered: Entire route in a generic public-health sense
sources.available_fields: Guidance text, threshold examples, reference links
sources.fallback_method: Seattle page or EPA AQI basics
sources.research_notes: Useful for static health guidance and rider copy references. Not a connector because it does not provide machine-readable current route conditions.

sources.source_name: City of Seattle wildfire smoke safety page
route_points_sections_covered: UW / Burke-Gilman start segment only in a generic health-guidance sense
sources.fallback_method: King County page or EPA AQI basics
sources.research_notes: Useful guidance reference only. Not a monitoring connector.
